input.quote: provided that the payment by PB to SFJ of the amounts specified as being payable upon a given termination in Section 14.2 shall be in lieu of any claim for damages that SFJ may have arising out of or in connection with the circumstances that formed the basis for such termination.
input.rationale: Section 14.4.2 expressly characterises the Section 14.2 termination amounts as sums payable by PB "in lieu of any claim for damages" — i.e. liquidated damages payable by us, the Customer. Those amounts are formulaic and punitive rather than compensatory: 300% of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ on SFJ's termination for our breach (14.2.1), on our at-will termination (14.2.2), on SFJ's bankruptcy termination (14.2.5.2) and in the safety-concern cases (14.2.7); 150% on a Change of Control or compliance-breach termination (14.2.6, 14.2.8.1); and Development Costs plus 25% per annum interest where SFJ simply disagrees with a JSC decision (14.2.10). This fails the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and is far outside the fallback ceiling of an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount. We have not flagged the Section 6.7 Buy-Out Payments (an elective prepayment right that benefits us) or the Section 6.4 default interest, which are ordinary commercial mechanics rather than liquidated damages. Because deleting every 14.2 payment formula would require extensive collateral rewrites of the funding economics, we target the fallback with one surgical amendment to the exclusive-remedy proviso, which already opens with a "Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary" override so the retained 14.2 formulas are displaced rather than left contradictory.

proposal.summary: Cap PB's termination payments at a single early-termination fee of three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 14.4.2 makes the Section 14.2 termination amounts (up to 300% of Development Costs) liquidated damages payable by us in lieu of SFJ's damages claim. We have replaced that mechanic so the only liquidated amount we pay on termination is a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees, consistent with our position that we pay no liquidated damages or penalties.
